interpretation: Instruction: 'Pick the akita black bowl from table center and place it on the plate'. The target is obj8: the bowl in the middle of the table at about (0.586, -0.004), 11x11x5 cm, with a dark patterned interior and a thin yellow rim, between the stove and the plate. A second, identical bowl (obj9) sits at (0.678, 0.312) next to the cookie box, off-centre to the robot's left, so it is not 'from table center'. 'The plate' is obj10, the white plate with red stripes at (0.734, 0.025), 13.6 cm across, with a flat centre at about z=-0.004 rising to a rim at z=0.008. Goal: the centre bowl resting upright on the plate. Only mild ambiguity: in this render the bowls look silver-grey with black patterning rather than plain black, but both bowls are the same model and only one is at the table centre.
plan: The bowl (outer rim radius 5.6 cm) is wider than the gripper's 7.9 cm maximum, so I chose a top-down rim grasp: closing axis radial, one finger inside the bowl and one outside. I grasped the +y side of the rim at yaw -90 deg (fingers closing along world y). That is the wrist's current orientation, so no wrist rotation was needed, and it keeps the 20 cm-wide hand away from the cabinet, whose +y face is about 13 cm from the plate edge. A -y-side grasp would have put the hand into the cabinet when placing. Sequence: pre-grasp 7 cm above the rim, descend to TCP z=0.030 (about 1 cm below the rim top), close, lift about 9 cm, carry at constant height until the bowl's centre is over the plate centre, lower until the bowl's underside is about 1 cm above the plate, open, then retreat straight up. Two changes along the way. (1) The direct approach preview was refused: too fast, and joint 2 crossed 0 near a singularity while joints 1 and 3 had to swing. I routed it through a waypoint in the y=0 plane and slowed it to 13.5 s. (2) After the lift the bowl had slid to a lip grip and tilted about 15 deg, and perception dropped it as part of the robot. So I measured the hanging bowl from the raw point cloud and set the carry offset (bowl centre about 5.2 cm in -y of the TCP) and the release height (lowest point about 6.5 cm below the TCP) from that measurement rather than from the pre-grasp geometry.

steps.why: Know the robot, cameras, gripper and budget before planning.
steps.result: Panda 'capx_libero_panda', 7 joints. Cameras: agentview (scene, facing the robot) and robot0_eye_in_hand (wrist). Parallel-jaw gripper: stroke 0.08 m, max_width 0.079 m, closed_empty 0.985, held_below 0.95. 7990 steps at control_dt 0.05 s. TCP at (0.452, 0, 0.265), fingers closing along world y (finger yaw -90).

steps.what: Looked at both cameras, listed objects, annotated ids on agentview, rendered closeups of obj8 and obj10.
steps.why: Identify the target bowl and the plate.
steps.result: obj8 = table-centre bowl; obj9 = other bowl by the cookie box; obj10 = plate; obj6 = ramekin; obj11 = cookie box; obj7 = cabinet; obj2 = stove.

steps.what: Measured geometry from object points: rim circle, height profile, plate rim circle.
steps.why: Place the grasp and release poses precisely.
steps.result: Bowl centre (0.5855, -0.0044), outer rim radius 0.056, rim top z 0.040, base about -0.008, wall 4-5 mm sloping inward with depth. Plate centre (0.7344, 0.0252), radius 0.068. A first fit over all plate points was biased toward -x by 6 mm, so I used the rim-only fit.

steps.what: Inspected finger and hand collision spheres in the TCP frame.
steps.why: No tip_reach_m was given; needed to know how far the fingertips reach below the TCP.
steps.result: Finger spheres reach about 2.2 cm past the TCP along the approach axis. The hand body spans +/-0.11 m along the closing axis. The finger sphere model covers the whole region between the fingers, so finger-vs-bowl contacts at the grasp pose are artifacts.

steps.what: Previewed a direct move to pre-grasp and down to the rim.
steps.result: Refused: up to 2.8x too fast (needs >=15.6 s), and joint 2 passes near 0 (shoulder singularity) while the path also moves sideways.

steps.what: Executed a re-routed approach: via (0.56, 0, 0.16) in the y=0 plane, then to pre-grasp (0.5855, 0.0456, 0.10), 13.5 s, arm check_batch collision-free.
steps.why: Keep joints 1 and 3 still while joint 2 crosses 0, then move sideways.
steps.result: Done, 276 steps. The ./py cell's 120 s timeout cut off the wait (the sim runs slower than real time), but the motion completed; I waited again with a longer timeout. The wrist view showed the rim centred between the open fingers.

steps.what: Descended straight down to TCP z=0.030 (3 s).
steps.why: Put the fingers on either side of the rim, pads about 1 cm below the rim top.
steps.result: 66 steps, step 342. In the wrist and agentview images the inner finger is inside the bowl and the outer finger is over the table, with the rim between them.
Reading 0.904, below held_below 0.95, with a 7.7 mm gap: holding the wall. The wrist image shows the fingers pinching the rim. Step 372.

steps.what: Lifted straight up to TCP z=0.12 (4.5 s, slower than the 2.95 s minimum to protect the friction grip).
steps.why: Clear the plate rim, which is only 1.7 cm from the bowl's far edge.
steps.result: 96 steps, step 468. The bowl is in the air in both cameras. The reading rose to 0.956 (gap 3.5 mm): the bowl slid about 1 cm down to a lip grip and tilted about 15 deg (cloud: grip-side rim at z 0.12, far rim about 0.09, lowest point about 0.058). Re-perception dropped the held bowl as a segment hugging the robot.

steps.what: Measured the hanging bowl from the raw cloud() inside a box under the TCP, excluding the finger region.
steps.why: Perception no longer listed the bowl, and the tilt changed the offset and depth I had planned with.
steps.result: Bowl centre about 5.2 cm in -y of the TCP at the same x; lowest point about 6.5 cm below the TCP. Set the carry target to TCP = plate centre + (0, 0.052) = (0.7344, 0.0772).

steps.what: Carried the bowl at constant height (z=0.12) to above the plate, 14 s (minimum 10.9 s), arm collision-free.
steps.why: Move slowly so the lip grip does not slip; the bowl's lowest point stays about 5 cm above the plate rim.
steps.result: 286 steps, step 754. Grip steady at 0.9565. The lowest part of the bowl in the cloud was centred 1-2 mm from the plate centre; agentview showed the bowl over the plate.

steps.what: Lowered 5.0 cm to TCP z=0.0695 (4 s).
steps.why: Bring the bowl's underside to about 1 cm above the plate's flat centre (z -0.004) before releasing.
steps.result: 86 steps, step 840. The bowl's lowest visible point is at about z 0.007-0.010, hanging just above the plate in agentview; grip unchanged.

steps.what: Opened the gripper (1 s), then held 0.5 s.
steps.why: Release the bowl onto the plate and let it settle.
steps.result: 30 steps, step 870. The gripper reads 0.015 (open). The bowl dropped and levelled; in the wrist view it is a full circle on the plate with the red stripes visible around it.

steps.what: Retreated straight up to TCP z=0.20 (4 s), collision-free.
steps.why: Clear the fingers from the rim without disturbing the bowl (fingertips were about 1.4 cm above the rim after release).
steps.result: 86 steps, step 956. The bowl did not move.

steps.what: Verified the final state with fresh agentview and wrist images, a re-perception, a cloud rim fit and a closeup render, then called finish_episode.
steps.why: Check each part of the instruction before ending.
steps.result: Bowl upright on the plate. Rim circle centre (0.735, 0.041), 1.55 cm toward +y of the plate centre. Rim heights 0.045-0.050 by sector, a tilt of about 3 deg because one edge of the foot sits on the plate's rising rim area. The foot is entirely within the plate radius and the table-centre spot is empty. The other bowl, cookie box, ramekin, stove and cabinet are unchanged. Finished at step 956 of 7990.

key_images.caption: Start: perceived ids on agentview. obj8 is the table-centre bowl (target), obj9 the other bowl, obj10 the plate, obj7 the cabinet.
Wrist view at grasp height before closing: the bowl rim lies between the open fingers (inner finger over the bowl interior, outer finger over the table).
After closing: fingers pinch the +y rim; reading 0.904 (held).
After lifting to TCP z=0.12: bowl in the air, hanging about 15 deg tilted from a lip grip (reading 0.956).
Bowl carried at constant height to above the plate.
Lowered until the bowl's underside is about 1 cm above the plate, just before release.
Just after opening: the bowl has dropped onto the plate and levelled.
Final scene from agentview after retreating up: bowl on the plate, table centre empty, other objects unchanged.
Final wrist view from above: bowl sitting on the plate, slightly toward +y (image left) of the plate centre.
Final closeup renders: bowl and plate merged by perception into obj17; bowl upright on the plate.

diagnosis: I believe this succeeded; residual risks only. The bowl ended about 1.55 cm off the plate centre toward +y, the grip side, with about a 3 deg tilt from one foot edge resting on the plate's rising rim area. Its base is fully on the plate, so a careful observer would call it on the plate, but a strict centring criterion could object. The offset came from the grip: during the lift the bowl slid down to a 3.5 mm lip grip and hung about 15 deg tilted, and I aimed the release with the lowest-points centroid of the hanging bowl. That centroid is biased toward the low (-y) side, so the bowl's true centre was nearer the TCP than I estimated, and it also shifted toward +y as it levelled on release. Done again, I would estimate the hanging bowl's centre from its rim circle rather than its lowest points, aim the release about 1-1.5 cm further toward -y, and grasp a bit deeper (TCP about 1.5-2 cm below the rim top) so the pinch holds more wall and the bowl tilts less.
lessons: On this LIBERO Panda, Cartesian moves need far more time than a naive guess: about 10-15 s for 15-25 cm. Preview first and use min_duration with margin. Moving from home out to the table crosses joint 2 = 0; keep that crossing in the y=0 plane (via a waypoint), then move sideways.

The sim runs slower than real time: a 13.5 s motion took over 2 minutes of wall time. Run ./py with --timeout 600 or more for executes, and call ep.wait() again if a cell times out; the motion keeps running.

A top-down radial rim grasp on the LIBERO bowl (TCP about 1 cm below the rim top, centred on the wall) holds, but it slips to a lip grip and the bowl tilts about 15 deg when lifted. The reading then rises above held_below (0.956) even though the bowl is still held, so confirm with images, not the reading alone.
A held object drops out of objects() (treated as hugging the robot). Locate it with raw ep.cloud() points in a box under the TCP, excluding the finger region.
When placing a tilted, rim-held bowl, estimate its centre from the rim circle, not the lowest points, and expect it to shift slightly toward the grip side as it levels on release.
After placing, perception merges the bowl with the plate. Fit a circle to the cloud points above the plate's height to check the bowl's centre offset and tilt.
Pick the grasp side so the 20 cm-wide hand stays clear of tall fixtures at the place location (here the cabinet on the -y side).
